properties.description: tools/reflow2_init.py. `--remove` (with `--check`, a preview in the same words) deletes every kit file nobody edited — proven by the receipt's sha, by being byte-identical to what this kit writes for any harness, or by an intact reflow2 mark — and names each edited one it keeps; strips exactly the blocks the kit appended (.gitignore's ignore block, .gitattributes' merge=reflow2 note and line, the terminal route's [export] table in .reflow2.toml, the pointer line in every instruction file), deleting a file the kit created whole; rewrites .reflow2/kit-version.json as `removed` (date, kit, the kept files' shas so a later init still leaves them alone, no `harnesses`); and touches nothing else in .reflow2/. It names what it leaves on purpose (this machine's MCP config entries, the loop-nudge hooks, the clone's merge driver) and the machine files git no longer ignores. `why_not_an_update` refuses with the no-kit words (`no_kit_here`) when the receipt says removed or when none of the files it records is left; one file gone still updates. `resolve_harnesses` refuses a non-interactive run on a live receipt with no `harnesses` and names `--harness`; a first install with no answer still installs every MCP harness. The `reflow2` wrapper passes `init --remove` through unchanged; its help names it.
properties.name: `reflow2 init --remove` takes the kit out of one project and keeps its design; `update` never brings a removed kit back, and never installs every harness when the receipt names none
